default_class_assumption: LO206 Junior Light @ Mosport / MIKA (path to BSC Ontario wins)

dimensions.label: Track width usage
observable_signals: distance to white line/kerb at entry
good_cues: Full entry width then full exit
dimensions.briggs_note: Critical for min speed without power

example_feedback.high: Width looks intentional — you’re using the full road and protecting minimum speed.
example_feedback.mid: Entry width is okay, but exits still leave money on the table. Commit to the exit kerb on the next three corners that open onto straights.
example_feedback.low: You’re turning early and floating inside. Pick one corner and force full track-out for five laps — LO206 needs that exit speed.

dimensions.label: Turn-in timing
observable_signals: when wheel moves vs visual markers
dimensions.briggs_note: Early turn-in amplifies exit loss with low power

example_feedback.high: Turn-in patience is strong — apexes support the exit.
example_feedback.mid: A couple of early darts are killing exit. Delay turn-in about one kart length on your worst corner.
example_feedback.low: Early turn-in is the main time thief. Name a turn-in marker, then delay it one kart length for five laps and compare exit.

dimensions.label: Apex quality
observable_signals: kart position at max lock / closest inside
good_cues: Not chasing paint for its own sake

example_feedback.high: Apexes look like exit tools, not trophies — good.
example_feedback.mid: You’re hitting the inside but still lifting to get there. Let the apex come to you later.
example_feedback.low: Early apex + lift is stacking. Stop “kerb worship” — later apex, earlier throttle.

dimensions.label: Exit commitment
dimensions.briggs_note: Exit RPM is race currency on LO206

example_feedback.high: Exits are committed — you’re feeding throttle early and using the road.
example_feedback.mid: Throttle arrives late on one or two key corners. Aim for progressive full throttle as soon as the wheel starts unwinding.
example_feedback.low: Exit commitment is soft. LO206 races are won on exit RPM — one primary corner: earlier roll-on, full track-out, no lift.

mychron_signals: exit RPM rise rate after min speed
RPM at first full-throttle sample off apex
exit speed vs reference on same corner

dimensions.label: Braking aggressiveness
good_cues: Firm initial hit in a straight line

example_feedback.high: Initial brake hit looks firm and decisive.
example_feedback.mid: Brakes are a bit soft. Hit harder on the straight, then bleed — don’t stretch a gentle squeeze forever.
example_feedback.low: Soft brake + coast is costing you. Firm stop on the straight first, then release into the turn.

dimensions.label: Brake release / trail
dimensions.briggs_note: Rear-brake-only karts are sensitive on release

example_feedback.high: Trail release is clean — deceleration blends into rotation.
example_feedback.mid: There’s a flat coast shelf before turn-in. Keep a light trail instead of going to zero brake.
example_feedback.low: Snap release / coast is pushing the front. Treat trail as a release skill: firm hit, then progressive bleed into apex.

dimensions.label: Braking consistency

example_feedback.high: Brake markers are stacked — great consistency.
example_feedback.mid: Brake points wander a bit. Pick one visual reference and nail it for five laps.
example_feedback.low: Inconsistent braking is inventing a new lap every time. Name the marker out loud for three corners.

mychron_signals: decel slope consistency into same corner

example_feedback.high: Steering is quiet — minimal angle, clean unwind.
example_feedback.mid: A few mid-corner corrections are scrubbing speed. Hold one input longer before adjusting.
example_feedback.low: Sawing the wheel is scrubbing the tires. Drill: count “one” while holding mid-corner steering — less input, more speed.

example_feedback.high: Hands stay planted at 9-and-3.
example_feedback.mid: Hands migrate under load. Reset to 9-and-3 every straight.
example_feedback.low: Hand shuffle is costing precision. Lock 9-and-3 for a full session — no exceptions.

dimensions.label: Throttle smoothness
dimensions.briggs_note: Cooks tires and drops RPM on LO206

example_feedback.high: Throttle is progressive and you hold full cleanly.
example_feedback.mid: A few stabs on exit. Roll on once — don’t pump.
example_feedback.low: Throttle stabbing is heating the rears and killing RPM. One smooth roll-on to full; if it spins, you turned in too early or asked too soon.

mychron_signals: RPM flat-spot / wheelspin signature on exit

example_feedback.high: Rotation is controlled — settle, then drive out.
example_feedback.mid: Occasional rear step. Ease brake release a touch earlier or unwind sooner.
example_feedback.low: Snap rotation / panic inputs. Slow the hands, finish the trail gently, straighten earlier.

example_feedback.high: Eyes are ahead — inputs look anticipatory, not reactive.
example_feedback.mid: A few late reactions. Look to the exit earlier so hands follow eyes.
example_feedback.low: Target fixation is making you late. For three corners, name the next reference before you arrive.

example_feedback.high: Body is quiet in the seat — good weight transfer.
example_feedback.mid: Upper body moves more than needed. Relax shoulders; let the kart work.
example_feedback.low: Body thrash is unloading the tires. Quiet torso for five laps — inputs only through hands/feet.

dimensions.label: Following / draft use
good_cues: Closes for tow then peels for pass
dimensions.briggs_note: Passes often need tow in LO206

example_feedback.high: Draft use is smart — close for tow, peel with a plan.
example_feedback.mid: Gaps are a bit big to ever tow. Close earlier on the straight without unsettled bumper contact.
example_feedback.low: You’re either too far to tow or too close and unsettled. Practice gap control before attempting passes.

example_feedback.high: Passes are planned — inside owned, exit protected.
example_feedback.mid: A few half-alongside attempts. Present earlier or wait a corner; outside usually donates.
example_feedback.low: Dive-bombs / outside lunges aren’t sticking. Plan the pass a corner ahead: tow, own the inside before turn-in, protect exit.

example_feedback.high: Defense is selective and legal — you still race your exit.
example_feedback.mid: Covering early is fine; don’t give away exit speed every corner.
example_feedback.low: Over-defending is making you the slowest kart. Cover once early, then race your line — don’t gift a switchback.

example_feedback.high: Lap 1 is measured — you survived and gained cleanly.
example_feedback.mid: A bit greedy on cold tires. Survive first, attack once grip arrives.
example_feedback.low: Cold-tire aggression is high-risk. Prioritize clean exits on lap 1; the pass comes after tires wake up.

dimensions.label: Consistency
dimensions.briggs_note: Consistency wins mains in parity classes

example_feedback.high: Lines stack lap to lap — that’s how you win LO206 mains.
example_feedback.mid: Pace is there but variance is high. Repeat the same references for five laps.
example_feedback.low: Every lap is reinvented. Consistency first: same markers, same exits, then push.

dimensions.label: Tire management
dimensions.briggs_note: May need gearing chat (tag as setup)

example_feedback.high: You adapt as tires age — inputs stay smooth late in the run.
example_feedback.mid: Slides grow late. Soften exits and protect the rear sooner in the stint.
example_feedback.low: Tires are falling off and inputs aren’t adapting. Smooth earlier; if exits feel lazy across the field, consider a setup hypothesis (gearing), not just “push harder.”

dimensions.setup_hypothesis_hint: If exits feel lazy despite clean inputs, +1 rear tooth is a common LO206 tire-wear response (Swift).

dimensions.label: Wet adaptation
dimensions.briggs_note: Low power means wet mistakes stick until the next straight

example_feedback.high: Wet markers look adapted — earlier brakes, avoid painted kerbs.
example_feedback.mid: Still a bit dry-line in places. Move markers earlier and leave shiny paint alone.
example_feedback.low: Dry line in the wet is costly on LO206. Earlier brakes, smoother everything, skip painted kerbs.

drills.name: Later turn-in drill
drills.instruction: Pick one hairpin or slow corner. Delay turn-in by about one kart length for 5 laps. Compare exit speed and track-out.

drills.name: No-coast braking drill
drills.instruction: Eliminate the flat speed shelf before turn-in. Firm brake, then continuous release into the corner — no coast.

drills.name: Trail creep drill
drills.instruction: Deepen brake release about 1 m later per session while keeping the release progressive (no snap-off).

drills.name: Hands quiet drill
drills.instruction: Hold mid-corner steering and count “one” before any correction. Goal: less sawing, less scrub.

drills.name: Reference naming
drills.instruction: Driver must name the turn-in marker for 3 corners before/during the run.

drills.name: Racecraft practice session
drills.instruction: Dedicate a practice session to passes and defense, not lap time. Plan passes one corner ahead; own inside before turn-in.

setup_hypothesis_templates.message: Setup hypothesis (not driver blame): exits feel lazy — common LO206 response is +1 rear tooth to keep RPM in the ~5800–6100 band (Swift).

when: living on limiter on short tracks
setup_hypothesis_templates.message: Setup hypothesis: from the front or for a long main, −1 rear tooth (longer) can protect tires and top speed (Swift).

when: inconsistent drive out of slow corners
setup_hypothesis_templates.message: Setup hypothesis: check clutch health/engagement and install (must be locked against crank shoulder — Briggs/Klaus). Don’t assume it’s only technique.
Setup hypothesis: if video inputs look clean but pace is down, diagnose chassis/drivetrain before blaming the sealed engine (Klaus #12).

Setup hypothesis: Junior Light blue .520 is more restricted than yellow .570 — gear for the (earlier) power-band peak, not the 6150 ignition max (Klaus #7). Blue-slide dyno peak RPM is an open gap — do not invent.

Tire pressure (setup): log cold PSI before the run and hot PSI after. LO206 tire growth with heat changes effective gearing — if exits get looser late, check whether hot pressures climbed and whether you’re overheating the rears before you “try harder” (Swift tire-growth + tire-management cues). Confirm compound/pressure box against current MIKA / Mosport rules — don’t invent a number off telemetry alone.

Tire pressure (race/heat): if grip falls off and opposite-lock creeps up, treat hot pressure + tire cook as a setup conversation first. Longer gear (−1 rear tooth) sometimes saves the tire on long mains; pressure and ratio interact (Swift). Re-check cold set before the next heat.

Gear ratio flag (setup): LO206 Junior Light (blue .520″ slide #555734) — gear for the restricted power-band peak (earlier than yellow .570), not limiter ego (Klaus #7 applies harder). Do not invent a blue-slide dyno peak — confirm dyno/slide chart. +1 rear tooth if exits feel lazy / RPM soft; −1 if living on the limiter early or saving tires from the front (Swift methodology).
Setup hypothesis (clutch): RPM flare with lagging speed = late/long slip. Cool, clean contamination/glaze, check gearing/drag, then weaker springs or add balanced weights (Hilliard Flame guide).
Setup hypothesis (clutch): early grab / RPM drop on bite. Confirm freewheel & idle, then stronger springs / remove balanced weights (Hilliard Flame guide).

setup_hypothesis_templates.summary: Verify carb float height / fuel delivery per Briggs guide; no illegal jet changes (Junior Light carb lock #555726).
when_signals: elevated water/CHT with soft top end

setup_hypothesis_templates.summary: Understeer/push: widen front track one spacer step (or +caster per chassis chart) — one change.
when_signals: won't rotate with healthy exit RPM

setup_hypothesis_templates.summary: Snap oversteer/rear step: narrow rear slightly — one change; re-check pressures.

Next practice: pass/defense session. Own the inside before turn-in; protect exit after the pass.

setup_hypotheses.message: Setup hypothesis: from mid/back, +1–2 rear teeth can help early-lap acceleration (Swift) — separate from driving notes.

contact_position_penalty.rule: Officials may place an offender behind all drivers who lost positions from contact (on top of ASN 1-15 penalties: warning, 5 s min, black flag, last place, rear of grid next race, DQ). Factors: positional loss, severity/avoidability, mitigating/aggravating circumstances.

coaching_hooks.D15: A pass that involves contact and moves someone back can be undone or worse. Score contact passes as low regardless of position gained; cue: set it up a corner earlier and own the inside cleanly.
coaching_hooks.D16: Defend without causing contact — late, aggressive blocks that trigger contact risk the same position penalty.
coaching_hooks.D17: Lap-1 contact in a pack can cost more than the positions gained; survival + clean exits first.

push_back_bumper.rule: MIKA Supp Regs §15: GDS/ASN Bumper Rules remain unchanged (1 side in = 5 s; both sides in = 5 s). MIKA modifies to a warning for 1 side in (5 s for 2 sides) for Briggs Senior/Masters only. Quote: 'Cadet, Junior and all 2 stroke classes will follow the ASN regulations on the push back bumper.'
push_back_bumper.junior_light_note: Supp Regs §15 names Cadet/Junior (not 'Junior Light'/'JR LITE' explicitly). Eligible-class list separately includes Briggs Junior Light. Junior Light is not in the Senior/Masters warning exception. Coaching default: treat Junior Light as ASN 5 s (same as Junior) — flag that the bumper paragraph does not name Junior Light verbatim.

coaching_hooks.D14: Draft without bumping — displaced front fairing is a 5 s ASN penalty for Cadet/Junior per §15; apply same caution for Junior Light coaching copy (see junior_light_note).
